survivingClaim: For w = sinc(x/8)^8 and 3 <= H <= T^{7/8 - eps}, S_w(u) equals the finite prime sum of the classical smoothed explicit formula up to a remainder of about H(8H/T)^7 log T (no explicit constant). For n0+1 < H it is the single term -(H w^(0)/2pi) Lambda(n0)/sqrt(n0) with w^(0) = 12.0478. This was checked on zeta zeros at T = 1e3, 2.5e3, 5e3, 1e4, 2e4. It vanishes at non-prime-powers for every Euler product and not for DH (b(6) = 1.936), so it uses the support of Lambda only. If exactly one off-line pair exists, |prime side| >= 2|W| sinh(delta u) - M_on; this lower bound is below the trivial Brun-Titchmarsh upper bound for every H, N and delta < 1/2 because N^delta < sqrt(N), so the route excludes nothing (classical trivial-strip obstruction). Measured, first order, T <= 3e4, H <= 10: the change in S_w on u <= theta log(T/2pi) from one off-line pair is reproduced by real displacements of neighbouring points for theta <= 0.45 and not for theta >= 0.5; the same holds for lattice and Poisson point sets, so it is a sampling-density statement. No statement about zeta zeros.
obstruction: One off-line pair of depth delta forces |short twisted prime sum| >= 2|W| sinh(delta log N) - M_on, which is below the trivial Brun-Titchmarsh upper bound for every H, N and delta < 1/2 since N^delta < sqrt(N). Closing the gap is the zero-free statement. Only the support and size of Lambda are used. Referee: obstruction stands; the claim as worded is false in three places (the identity has a remainder of about H(8H/T)^7 log T and needs H = o(T^(7/8))).

E1 (headline wording). The identity is not "exact with no H-dependent error". The remainder R is nonzero, about H(8H/T)^7 log T, because the sinc^8 window decays only like x^-8 (mirrored zeros and the archimedean singularity near t = 0). It tends to 0 only for H = o(T^{7/8}). lesson: Window-local explicit-formula identities are exact, so there is no error term to beat. The comparison that matters is off-line amplitude N^delta against the trivial sqrt(N) bound on short twisted prime sums, and closing that gap is the zero-free statement itself. Only prime-power support and the size of Lambda are used (inputs the sign twists keep); multiplicativity of the test polynomial D gives no gain. Every control with a symmetric zero side fails only at size or support; the Liouville twist passes every step. The averaged form is MV-CAP (P27, Q9, Z17); the single-window form stops at the Re s = 1 wall (P29).
followUp: none of high value. The only adjacent option, N between T^(1/2) and T where the measured residual is O(1), needs the same bound on short twisted prime sums. The absorbability thresholds (1/2 and 1) are float64, first-order, band-truncated measurements at T <= 3e4; an interval-arithmetic recheck would be needed before they are cited as filters.
